In #7171 `graal-sdk` got split into several parts. This patch accounts for that and adds
the new dependencies to the module path when the JDKs `jimage` is being queried for built-in modules.

`--add-modules org.graalvm.polyglot` has been dropped from the native-image launcher. It
gets added to the module path on demand if needed.

Closes #7085

There is similar logic already implemented in https://github.com/oracle/graal/blob/e4935fced6c03774fd0167dced8cdce32df3f817/substratevm/src/com.oracle.svm.driver/src/com/oracle/svm/driver/NativeImage.java#L1030C5-L1035

```suggestion
                result.addAll(getJars(libJvmciDir, "enterprise-graal"));
```

To my understanding [`graal-sdk` is now obsolete](https://github.com/oracle/graal/pull/7171#issue-1843030913)

I believe we can add `polyglot` (and possibly `truffle-api`) here and if detected subsequently pass `add-modules` as well.

If I am not mistaken this would remove the need to have it hardcoded in `mx_sdk_vm_impl.py`.

What's the command you are using to build GraalVM in this case? If `polyglot` is not part of the dependencies then not copying `polyglot.jar` over is correct.

E.g.

```
mx --primary-suite-path substratevm --no-jlinking --components="Native Image,LibGraal" --native-images=native-image,lib:jvmcicompiler build
```

Shouldn't copy `polyglot.jar`.

On the other hand:

```
mx --primary-suite-path substratevm --no-jlinking --components="Native Image,LibGraal,poly" --native-images=native-image,lib:jvmcicompiler build
```

Should probably copy it over.

Is because we explicitly pass `--add-modules org.graalvm.polyglot` to the command line despite `polyglot.jar` not being present (or needed).

Yes.

> and the launcher script referencing it using `--add-modules`.

Exactly, that's the issue. That's why I believe we should remove it from the bash/native launcher and have `NativeImage` add it only when necessary as I think the launcher doesn't really need it...

This didn't fail with the earlier patch as not all options got passed whole-sale to the `list-modules` call. So there are a couple of options how to fix it:

1. Silence unified logging for the `-XX:StartFlightRecording=dumponexit=true` test with `-Xlog:jfr\*=off`
2. Go back to the previous version of the patch (only passing `--upgrade-module`  option when needed)
3. Fix `callListModules` routine to ignore such unexpected output.

Which one should it be?

>  1.   Silence unified logging for the -XX:StartFlightRecording=dumponexit=true test with -Xlog:jfr\*=off
>  2.  Go back to the previous version of the patch (only passing --upgrade-module option when needed)
>  3.  Fix callListModules routine to ignore such unexpected output.
> Which one should it be?

Please go for `3`.

IMO, `2.` is not an option because there might be `javaArgs` used by the builder that influence the output of `--list-modules`. E.g. `--patch-module`, `--enable-preview` ... we want our `--list-modules` query to run in the same JVM context that be builder is also running afterwards.

The reason is that the `-J--limit-modules=org.graalvm.nativeimage.builder` constrains the builder down to the transitive closure of the module org.graalvm.nativeimage.builder (itself + all modules it depends on).

But luckily we do have our `--list-modules` option implemented in the builder. So instead of using the  `--list-modules` option implemented in `java` use our version, then `-J--limit-modules=org.graalvm.nativeimage.builder` cannot hurt the `org.graalvm.nativeimage.librarysupport` module the the builder requires (it contains that `com.oracle.svm.thirdparty.gson.GsonFeature`). Run
```
mx native-image -J--limit-modules=org.graalvm.nativeimage.builder --list-modules
```
to see what I mean (and compare it to the output of `callListModules`.

> Is that still the right reproducer?

Yes, `com.oracle.svm.polyglot.groovy.GroovyIndyInterfaceFeature` is the other feature that is packed in `library-support.jar` (alongside `com.oracle.svm.thirdparty.gson.GsonFeature`).

> Adding the -J--limit-modules=org.graalvm.nativeimage.builder parameter, seems to cause the driver to omit -imagemp <path/to/library-support.jar>

Exactly. That's because the output of `--list-modules` when combined with `--limit-modules=org.graalvm.nativeimage.builder` will not show `library-support.jar` anymore because it's not part of the transitive dependencies of `org.graalvm.nativeimage.builder`.

As already hinted, using the `--list-modules` of the native-image builder itself does not suffer from that problem.

> As already hinted, using the --list-modules of the native-image builder itself does not suffer from that problem.

You will have to use the raw-variant `-H:+ListModules` instead of the `--list-modules` when you uase it as `imageArgs`.
